questions.prompt: Gradient descent runs on f(θ)=½λθ² with learning rate η. For which η do the iterates converge to the minimum?
options: Any η > 0, because the gradient always points downhill
questions.explanation: θ_{t+1}=(1−ηλ)θ_t converges iff |1−ηλ|<1, i.e. 0<η<2/λ. The direction is downhill, but a long step can overshoot by more than it started with.

questions.prompt: f(θ)=½λθ² with λ=10. Start at θ₀=2 and take one gradient-descent step with η=0.15. What is θ₁? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
questions.explanation: θ₁=(1−0.15·10)·2=(−0.5)·2=−1. The sign flips because ηλ>1 but ηλ<2, so it still converges.

questions.prompt: N=5000 training samples, batch size 96, the short last batch is kept. How many parameter updates are in one epoch? (integer, tolerance 0.01)
questions.explanation: 5000/96=52.08, rounded up to 53: 52 full batches (4992 samples) plus one batch of 8.

questions.prompt: A ReLU layer has 200 inputs. What standard deviation does He initialization use for its weights? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
Every weight in a hidden layer is initialized to the same constant value. What goes wrong?
options: The learning rate must be doubled to compensate, since identical units learn at half speed.
All hidden units receive identical gradients and stay identical, so the layer acts like one unit.
The network cannot compute a forward pass, because identical weights make activations undefined.
All gradients in the output layer are exactly zero, so no weight ever updates at all.
questions.explanation: Symmetry: identical weights give identical activations and identical backward signals, so the updates never differentiate them.

questions.prompt: Minibatch size is multiplied by 4 with everything else fixed. What happens to the standard deviation of the minibatch gradient noise?
options: It is unchanged, because the gradient is unbiased.
questions.explanation: Noise std scales as σ/√B, so B×4 gives half the std. Unbiasedness says nothing about the variance.

questions.prompt: You must decide between learning rates 0.1 and 0.01 for a small network. Describe an experiment whose conclusion another person could rerun and reject: what do you fix, what do you vary, what do you report, and what result would reject your conclusion?
rubric: Fixes seed(s), data split, batch size, epoch budget and metric; changes only the learning rate.
Chooses on a validation set, repeats over several seeds, and reports spread, not a single run.
Names a falsifier, e.g. the ranking flips on another split or the gap is below the seed spread.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
